# 02-acting-and-tools - Acting and tools

## Why this topic exists

An agent is a model that can act. This topic is about the loop that interleaves a reasoning step with a tool call and feeds the result back, which is the structure underneath every agent in this library. It also covers the separate question of where tool-calling ability comes from, as distinct from how a tool interface is designed.

## Prerequisite topics

- [`01-reasoning`](../01-reasoning/README.md) Reasoning

## Papers in this topic

### ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu and others (2022)

- arXiv: [2210.03629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- PDF: [`2210.03629-react.pdf`](pdf/2210.03629-react.pdf)
- Notes: [`2210.03629-react.md`](notes/2210.03629-react.md)
- Tier: core, read first

Read this as the direct ancestor of the agent loop: reasoning and acting placed in one alternating cycle.

### Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

Timo Schick, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Roberto Dessì and others (2023)

- arXiv: [2302.04761](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)
- PDF: [`2302.04761-toolformer.pdf`](pdf/2302.04761-toolformer.pdf)
- Notes: [`2302.04761-toolformer.md`](notes/2302.04761-toolformer.md)
- Tier: deep, read after the core paper in its topic

Read this for the question of where tool-calling ability comes from, as distinct from how a tool interface is designed.
